To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed and implemented a new distributed CDMA/OFS code assignment algorithm for wireless ad hoc network modelled by unit-disk graph.
we present several distributed CDCA/OVSF code allocation algorithms for wireless ad-hoc networks modelled by UG, with provable performance guarantees.
we have given several distributed CDMA code assignment algorithms for ad hoc wireless networks that can approximate the optimum in terms of the total throughput, minimum rate and the sum of the two.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problems: (1) Given a UDG, find a distributed method such as to minimize the maximum rate of all the nodes in the graph.
the design of distributed code assignment algorithms for ad hoc wireless networks.

the following two issues: (1) How to design a code assignment algorithm such that the total throughput achieved is within a factor of the optimum; (2) How to design code assignment algorithms such that the minimum throughput achieved is within some factor of the optimum, and the total throughput achieved can also be approximated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the distributed algorithms presented here are theoretically good for wireless ad hoc network modelled by UDC.
the distributed algorithms presented in this paper can be used in a practical system.
our distributed code assignment algorithm is theoretically good and can be practically implemented.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the first time, we show that the OVSF codes can be used for distributed CDMA code assignment in wireless ad hoc networks.
we give several distributed methods that can achieve a near-optimum throughput and/or minimum rate in a wireless network of n mobile nodes.
we present a set of theoretically good distributed code assignment algorithms for UDG modelled ad hoc wireless networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distributed methods we present can be used to achieve good throughput in wireless networks.
the CDMA/OVSFs can be assigned in a distributed manner such that the performance is close to the optimum.
distributed code assignment for ad hoc networks is possible and can be done efficiently.
